author: ACA
what_it_is: Game fully completed with a score of 101%!
format: DexDrive .n64: "123-456-STD" and a 0x1040-byte header (DexPlorer comments), then a 32 KiB Controller Pak with one GameShark cart-save note "DODO" (3BADD1E5/FADE), 7 pages = the first 1792 bytes of the 16 Kbit EEPROM (trailing padding page dropped); ID block checksums 0101/FEFD

verified.converted_with: tools/gamefaqs/n64-dexdrive.py convert donkey-kong-64.1156.n64 OUT: dexdrive: pak = the 32768 bytes after the 0x1040-byte header; ID block checksums 0101/FEFD wrong in every copy, rewritten as 0101/FEF1; cart-save note 'DODO' (GameShark 3BADD1E5/FADE): raw EEPROM, 1792 bytes, padded with 00 to 2048

converted_standalone.how: the same bytes as the .srm regions, as standalone Mupen64Plus keeps them: <GoodName (32 chars)>-<MD5 8>.eep/.sra/.fla/.mpk in its save folder

verified.baseline: with no save: the file barrel reads EMPTY, and A starts a new game (GAME 1, 0%, 000:00)

mupen64plus-next.detail: file barrel GAME 1, then 101%, 201 golden bananas, 033:32, all five Kongs: as described (101%)

parallel-n64.detail: file barrel GAME 1, then 101%, 201 golden bananas, 033:32, all five Kongs: as described (101%)

mupen64plus.detail: file barrel GAME 1, then 101%, 201 golden bananas, 033:32, all five Kongs: as described (101%)

note: A GameShark cart-save note holding a 16 Kbit EEPROM without its last (padding) page; the converter pads it with 00 to 2048 bytes as save-file-converter does. The pak's ID block checksums are DexPlorer's (FEFD) and were rewritten, though only the EEPROM matters for this game.
